content.title: Is Senate voting today to end shutdown 2026? ICE, TSA airport updates
content.text: March 23, 2026, 4:39 p.m. ETAfter a rare Sunday session in which it met from noon to 4 p.m., the Senate reconvened Monday afternoon as we inch closer to the longest government shutdown in history, partial shutdowns included.Now 37 days into the shutdown 2026 today, Monday, March 23, a Senate vote to end the DHS shutdown and fully reopen the government is unlikely as hours-long TSA wait times are reported and President Donald Trump deploys ICE to airports.According to reports, Senate Majority Leader John Thune met with President Donald Trump to discuss a proposal to fund all of DHS except U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), following a push by some GOP senators.If this compromise would be put forward by Senate GOP, it would address the Democrats' demands that ICE and Border Patrol be reined in, a major cause of the bitter bipartisan battle that has raged for weeks on Capitol Hill in the wake of ICE's fatal shootings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good in Minnesota in January.The latest shutdown news today comes after a fatal airplane crash at LaGuardia Airport, which closed but has since reopened, and an expected Senate vote today to confirm Sen. Markwayne Mullin, a Republican from Oklahoma, as the new DHS secretary, following the firing of Kristi Noem in early March.The partial government shutdown began Feb. 14 after the Senate failed to approve funding for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). Since then, the Senate has failed four times to reach the 60 votes needed to end the shutdown. Sen. John Fetterman, a Pennsylvania Democrat, has been the lone "yes" vote across party lines.With spring break travel underway, March Madness fans traveling to NCAA basketball games, and heightened US security concerns over the Iran war, TSA wait times at Atlanta, Houston, New Orleans, and JFK airports turned chaotic with more than a third of TSA officers calling out of work, per CBS News. As TSA agents go without full paychecks, CEOs at major airports United, American, JetBlue, and Southwest have urged Congress to restore DHS funding to allow TSA workers to get paid.Trump sent ICE agents to the three major NYC-area airports today — LaGuardia, JFK, Newark — with agents headed to or already spotted at Philadelphia (PHL), Pittsburgh, Southwest Florida, Phoenix Sky, Atlanta, Houston, New Orleans, Cleveland (CLE), Chicago-O'Hare, and Luis Munoz Marin (SJU) in Puerto Rico. It's unclear how many ICE agents are at each airport.Despite the growing DHS shutdown risks to TSA, FEMA, the Coast Guard and Cybersecurity, lawmakers have continued trading blame in heated exchanges live on the Senate floor, led by Majority Leader John Thune, a South Dakota Republican, and Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, a New York Democrat.During a live Senate hearing on Saturday, Schumer brought forward a motion to pay TSA, splitting a proposed measure from funding ICE and Border Patrol, but it was met with intense scrutiny from Thune and other Republicans. Schumer said he was "disturbed" that "untrained ICE agents" would be "lurking at our airports." Some have taken to X to post photos showing ICE agents "hovering" over TSA agents, drawing ire and confusion over the purpose of ICE at airports."Even worse, they have no plan for using these ICE agents," Schumer said, adding, "Another impulsive action by Donald Trump. Whenever Donald Trump acts impulsively with no follow through, there’s trouble."Thune said the White House has offered "substantial" reforms to Democrats' ICE demands, casting blame on Democrats for the shutdown as a political pawn to "serve their political ends."The latest DHS shutdown updates come amid a possible full Senate vote on the SAVE Act, Trump's 2026 legislation which would require proof of citizenship to register to vote and photo ID to cast a ballot. Trump has pressed Republicans to pass the SAVE America Act before the midterms, but it is not likely to survive a full vote.Does the Senate vote today? When does Senate vote again on government shutdown 2026?Yes, the Senate is expected to vote today, Monday, March 23, but a vote to reopen the government is not expected. Instead, the Senate returned at 3 p.m. ET to potentially confirm the nomination of Sen. Markwayne Mullin as new DHS secretary, replacing since-fired Kristi Noem.The Senate will likely engage in heated debate over the DHS shutdown, DHS funding lapse and its impact at major airports, with TSA agent pay dwindling to partial paychecks. However, Trump has urged Republican lawmakers to focus on passing the SAVE America Act, with lawmakers spending a rare weekend in session to debate Trump's legislation ahead of the midterm elections. It's unlikely the SAVE Act passes a full Senate vote.What time is next Senate vote?The Senate returns at 3 p.m. ET today but a Senate vote to end the government shutdown is not expected today, with odds slim the DHS shutdown 2026 ends today. Impacts of the partial government shutdown have hit major airports, with Trump deploying ICE agents and TSA wait times ticking up among TSA PreCheck and general security lines.It's expected that a Senate vote today to confirm new DHS secretary, Sen. Markwayne Mullin, will take place after 3 p.m. ET, and likely before 7:43 p.m., when debate is set to expire.How to watch Senate vote live; Senate live streamA Senate vote to confirm the nomination of Markwayne Mullin, the new DHS secretary is expected live on the Senate floor today. However, a vote to end the shutdown is unlikely when the Senate returns at 3 p.m. ET. Senate floor proceedings stream live at Senate.gov. To watch Senate hearings from this week, head to C-SPAN, who also provides full transcripts of Senate hearings.You can watch live coverage of Senate sessions on C-SPAN on cable TV. C-SPAN livestreams on several streaming platforms including FuboTV, Philo, Hulu + Live TV, DIRECTV, and YouTube TV. What time is DHS secretary confirmation? Where to watchA Senate vote today to confirm Sen. Markwayne Mullin as the new DHS secretary is expected to take place live on the Senate floor between 3 p.m. ET and 7:43 p.m. — the time cloture debate expires. Trump's pick comes following his firing of former DHS secretary Kristi Noem on March 5. To watch the Senate vote today, head to the Senate livestream here.Why is DHS still shut down? Why is the government shutdown right now?The DHS shutdown 2026 continues today amid several failed Senate votes between Senate Democrats and Senate Republicans to pass a DHS funding bill that would restore monies in the DHS 2026 budget to pay 100,000+ workers within DHS agencies, many of whom are working without pay, particularly at airports where a TSA staffing crisis is playing out amid spring break travel, a fatal crash at LaGuardia airport, and long TSA wait times stretching for hours in major airports like Atlanta, JFK and Houston. Fears remain heightened amid security concerns as the Iran war carries on today.ICE, Border Patrol, and the Coast Guard, however, remain fully funded due to other funds or from Trump's signature $170 billion One Big Beautiful Bill.When will the partial government shutdown end? How long is the government shutdown going to last?The partial government shutdown, which is impacting DHS agencies only, ends when the next Senate vote passes with the 60 votes needed. The last vote to end the shutdown, on Thursday, March 12, failed 51-46 live on the Senate floor that would have reopened the Department of Homeland Security. Pennsylvania Senator John Fetterman was the lone Democrat to vote "yes."During a long weekend session, lawmakers failed to take up a motion by Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer that would have funded TSA agents only, pushing aside funding for ICE and Border Patrol. Odds the shutdown carries into day 38 tomorrow are high as lawmakers focus on debating the SAVE America Act and confirming the DHS secretary nomination today.What DHS departments are affected by DHS shutdown? DHS funding lapseTSA, FEMA, and Cybersecurity are among the DHS agencies affected by the DHS funding lapse. ICE, Border Patrol and the Coast Guard are receiving funding through various means, including Trump's signature $170 billion One Big Beautiful Bill.Some 50,000 TSA agents at major airports are working without pay or receiving partial pay as "essential" workers amid the DHS funding lapse within the DHS budget 2026. FEMA disaster relief funds for states have dwindled, Senate Majority Leader John Thune has said.Here's who else is affected by the government shutdown.Are air traffic controllers getting paid right now? Is TSA not getting paid?Air traffic controllers are being paid since they fall under the Department of Transportation; however, TSA agents are only receiving partial paychecks since they fall under the DHS agencies impacted by the partial government shutdown.When was the last government shutdown?The last government shutdown in 2025 was 43 days and considered the longest shutdown in history, stretching from Oct. 1, 2025, to Nov. 12, 2025. Senate Democrats and Republicans, including President Donald Trump, failed to agree on a short-term deal to keep the government funded, only passing (temporary) funding bills through Jan. 30.We are currently in the second-longest federal government shutdown in history; Under President Donald Trump's first term, the now-third-longest shutdown lasted a full 34 days, from Dec. 22, 2018, through Jan. 22, 2019.Senate scheduleThe U.S. Senate is on recess starting March 30 for the Easter holiday, not returning until April 13, barring any changes to the legislative calendar. The Senate schedule shows lawmakers typically tend to formal business, or are in session, around 140 of 165 days annually. These are "legislative" days when the U.S. Senate convenes to debate bills, vote, or conduct floor business.Unlike traditional jobs, a legislative day can last longer than 24 hours or stretch across multiple calendar days, and senators are usually occupied year-round with other responsibilities. Here's the official 2026 Senate schedule.Lori Comstock is a New Jersey-based journalist with the Mid-Atlantic Connect Team.
